x_1577958_dsb_pattern.name: Enterprise integrations (IntegrationHub, SAP, Workday, Salesforce)
x_1577958_dsb_pattern.overview: Register, standardise, secure, monitor. (1) Build the integration register from evidence int.inventory and interviews: owner, direction, system of record, objects, volume, SLA, method. (2) Standard: spoke first; custom IntegrationHub action with connection alias second; scripted REST only with justification. (3) Credentials in credential/connection aliases (or external vault); OAuth for inbound; IP access control. (4) Standard error handling subflow: retry with back-off, dead-letter record, incident to owner. (5) Refactor high-risk scripts (int.risk) in priority order. (6) Monitoring dashboard and alerts; IntegrationHub transaction consumption reviewed monthly. (7) Contract tests in ATF for critical integrations using mock responses where possible.
x_1577958_dsb_pattern.pain: Point-to-point scripts with hard-coded endpoints and credentials Failures discovered by users days later No inventory or owner for integrations Upgrades break custom SOAP/REST scripts Duplicate data because system-of-record boundaries are unclear
x_1577958_dsb_pattern.summary: Integrations have grown point-to-point: scripted REST calls with hard-coded endpoints and credentials, silent failures, no retry, and no owner. Upgrades break them and nobody knows which are still used. The pattern converges on a governed integration layer: an integration inventory with owners, IntegrationHub spokes and Flow Designer actions in preference to scripts, connection and credential aliases, standard error handling and retry, monitoring and alerting, and a contract per integration (direction, system of record, volume, SLA).
